parts.t: Calculate the height VO of the pyramid.
Calculate the angle between the edge VA and the base ABCD.
Calculate the angle between the face VBC and the base ABCD.

the diagonals of a square bisect each other
AO is the projection of AV on the base, so the required angle is angle VAO.
Let M be the midpoint of BC. Then VM ⊥ BC and OM ⊥ BC, so the angle between the face and the base is angle VMO.

The face DCFE is a vertical rectangle with CF = 4 cm, and ABFE is a sloping rectangle.

parts.t: Calculate the angle between AF and the base ABCD.
Calculate the angle between the sloping face ABFE and the base ABCD.

sols: CF is vertical, so AC is the projection of AF on the base and the required angle is angle FAC in the right-angled triangle ACF.
The two faces meet along AB. BC lies in the base and BF lies in the sloping face, and both are perpendicular to AB, so the angle between the faces is angle FBC.

Kai walks 40 m from P directly towards the mast to a point Q, where the angle of elevation of T is 47°.

parts.t: Use the sine rule in triangle PQT to calculate QT.
Calculate the height of the mast.

sols: angles in triangle PQT; equivalently the exterior angle 47° = 28° + angle PTQ
QT is opposite the 28° angle at P, and PQ = 40 m is opposite the 19° angle at T.
In the right-angled triangle QFT, TF is opposite the 47° angle and QT is the hypotenuse.
Height of the mast = 42.2 m (3 s.f.)
check: 42.18 ÷ tan 47° = 39.3 and 42.18 ÷ tan 28° = 79.3, which differ by 40 ✓
ms: B1 for 180 − 47 = 133 and 180 − 28 − 133 = 19, or 47 − 28 = 19 with exterior angle stated

M1 for their QT × sin 47 oe
A1
